title: Un verre d'eau  (A Glass of Water)

segments.t: Catching her breath in her office chair, pregnant agent Andrea receives a glass of water from loyal colleague Gabriel. As her physical discomfort subsides, Gabriel urges her to moderate her intense working schedule for her child's sake. Let's listen to their intimate conversation in French first.
Voici ton verre d'eau fraîche, Andréa.
C'est bon, la contraction est passée.
Bois un peu d'eau, doucement.
Merci Gabriel, je me sens déjà mieux.
Tu as souvent de telles douleurs?
Parfois, quand je marche trop vite.
Tu devrais vraiment ralentir le rythme.
Impossible avec tous mes rendez-vous importants!
La santé de ton bébé passe avant.
Je le sais bien, mon cher Gabriel.
Promets-moi de te reposer ce soir.
D'accord, je vais rentrer plus tôt.
Je surveillerai ton départ du bureau.
Tu es vraiment un ami formidable!

'It is fine, the contraction has passed.' The verb meaning 'passed' pairs naturally with the noun for 'uterine contraction' in everyday conversation.

'Thank you Gabriel, I already feel better.' The short 'self' word sits right in front of the verb for 'feel', turning the action back onto the subject.

'Sometimes, when I walk too fast.' The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'walk'.

'You should really slow down the pace.' A conditional modal advising professional restraint. The informal 'you' form around 'should' marks a direct, personal relationship.

'I know it well, my dear Gabriel.' A concession acknowledging sincere advice. The descriptive adjective for 'dear' agrees in gender and number with its noun.

'Promise me to rest tonight.' Notice how 'promise me' leads directly into the noun meaning 'evening hours'. Notice how 'promise me' leads directly into the noun meaning 'evening hours'.

'All right, I am going to go home earlier.' An agreeing near-future commitment to rest. Notice how 'am going' leads directly into the noun meaning 'agreement'.
